description: Tony's working directory of agent-operable tools, standards, runtimes, hosted AI and model platforms, communication layers, payment protocols, commerce platforms, CRM/customer systems, web analytics, control planes, and observability surfaces. Entries belong here when agents can use, configure, update, maintain, observe, or control them through documented agentic surfaces, not merely because humans can view them. Six review-recommended entries from the 21 May 2026 validation report are removed pending stronger verification. Data-residency posture was added on 14 June 2026 as conservative field notes, not compliance advice. Treat entries as field notes and leads, not endorsements or a complete public registry.
inclusion_bar: Tools with both a human view and an agentic operating surface, where the agent view is equal to or more powerful than the human view.
Products agents can configure, update, maintain, observe, or control through documented APIs, MCP servers, CLIs, webhooks, configuration files, SDKs, or equivalent automation surfaces.
Agent runtimes and harnesses that inspect projects, edit files, run commands, call tools, and execute multi-step workflows.
Protocols and standards that let agents discover instructions, use tools, communicate with other agents, interact with UIs, or transact safely.
Hosted AI and model platforms that agents call for inference, tool use, embeddings, multimodal generation, or managed GPU/app execution.
Control planes, dashboards, bridges, observability tools, session browsers, payment rails, commerce platforms, CRM connectors, web analytics, and usage monitors designed around agentic workflows.

entries.agent_native_scope: Lets agents and agent frameworks call Stripe APIs, create payment links, work with MCP, and build agentic commerce flows.
entries.summary: Stripe tooling for agentic workflows, including the Agent Toolkit, MCP server, AI docs, and agentic commerce guides.
entries.security_notes: Use restricted Stripe keys, scoped permissions, explicit human mandates, spending limits, audit logs, and test mode before any live-money workflow.

data_residency.label: Verify vendor
data_residency.note: Stripe documents transfer frameworks, but this pass did not verify a simple EU/US storage choice for agent tooling.

entries.name: Shopify Storefront Catalog MCP

entries.summary: Official Shopify MCP surface for storefront catalog search and product discovery, aligned with UCP catalog capabilities.
entries.security_notes: Catalog discovery is lower risk than checkout, but product metadata, inventory, pricing, and storefront access still need merchant approval and rate limits.

data_residency.label: Europe + global
data_residency.note: Shopify stores certain merchant/customer personal data in Europe while operating global transfer controls.

entries.name: PayPal Agent Toolkit

entries.summary: PayPal toolkit for integrating PayPal APIs into AI agent workflows across MCP and popular agent frameworks.
entries.security_notes: PayPal tools can touch live orders, invoices, subscriptions, disputes, and credentials. Use sandbox mode, scoped apps, approvals, and transaction limits.

data_residency.label: Verify vendor
data_residency.note: PayPal has regional privacy terms, but this pass did not verify a clear EU/US storage selector for the agent toolkit.

entries.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce

entries.summary: Visa program and pilot developer tooling for trusted agentic commerce, tokenized payments, and payment-enabled agent workflows.
entries.security_notes: Pilot and partner access may apply. Treat as high-trust payment infrastructure: verify eligibility, tokenization, identity, audit, and user consent flows.

data_residency.label: Hosted: verify

data_residency.label: Hosted: verify
data_residency.note: Hosted service; no official residency claim verified in this pass.

entries.summary: Adyen agentic commerce materials and ecosystem participation around AI-led checkout, merchant payments, and AP2 collaboration.
entries.security_notes: Good strategic signal, but verify concrete APIs, regional availability, and production integration paths before listing as an installable agent tool.

data_residency.label: Europe primary
data_residency.note: Adyen says payments processed are stored in Europe and an isolated India environment; systems also run in several regions.

entries.name: BigCommerce AI-ready Developer Docs
entries.agent_native_scope: Gives agents API documentation, llms.txt indexes, and commerce APIs for storefront, catalog, checkout, orders, customers, and integrations.
entries.summary: BigCommerce developer docs and APIs are increasingly agent-readable, including llms.txt, page-level Markdown, API runner, and store management APIs.
entries.security_notes: Not a dedicated agent product. Treat store API credentials as privileged access to catalog, orders, customers, checkout, and settings.

data_residency.label: Hosted: verify
data_residency.note: Hosted service; no official residency claim verified in this pass.

entries.name: Salesforce Agentforce

entries.summary: Salesforce platform for CRM-native AI agents, with developer APIs, SDKs, architecture guidance, and customer-success workflows.
entries.security_notes: Deep CRM access needs strict profile/permission design, data-governance review, audit logging, approvals, and clear human escalation paths.

data_residency.label: Region choice
data_residency.note: Salesforce Hyperforce provides local data storage/residency choices; confirm product and org region.

entries.name: HubSpot MCP Server

entries.summary: Official remote MCP server for bringing HubSpot CRM context into AI agents and third-party applications.
entries.security_notes: Scope the connected HubSpot app carefully. CRM data includes contacts, companies, deals, notes, and possibly sensitive customer history.

data_residency.label: EU/US + more
data_residency.note: HubSpot accounts are hosted in selected regional data centers including US and EU Germany.

entries.name: Zendesk AI Agents

entries.summary: Zendesk developer surface for AI agents in customer service and support automation workflows.
entries.security_notes: Support agents can expose customer tickets and account data. Use API-key hygiene, role limits, handoff rules, and conversation audit trails.

data_residency.label: EU/US + more
data_residency.note: Zendesk offers regional hosting for entitled customers, including US and EEA choices.

entries.name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Agents
entries.agent_native_scope: Uses Dynamics 365 and Copilot Studio agents for sales, service, finance, operations, contact center, and customer journeys.
entries.summary: Microsoft Dynamics 365 agent and Copilot capabilities across CRM, ERP, contact center, and Customer Insights workflows.
entries.security_notes: Dynamics agents may span CRM, ERP, Teams, finance, and service records. Confirm environment boundaries, data-loss prevention, and approval paths.

data_residency.label: Azure geo choice
data_residency.note: Dynamics 365 stores customer data at rest in the selected Azure geo, with EU Data Boundary commitments.

entries.name: ServiceNow AI Agent Studio
entries.agent_native_scope: Creates, manages, tests, and observes AI agents and agentic workflows across ServiceNow business processes.
entries.summary: ServiceNow studio for building and managing self-executing AI agents and agentic workflows inside the ServiceNow platform.
entries.security_notes: Enterprise workflow agents can mutate tickets, cases, HR records, approvals, and operational processes. Start with narrow actions and observable test runs.

data_residency.label: Region choice
data_residency.note: ServiceNow has EU hosting options and AI data residency controls; confirm contract/product scope.

entries.agent_native_scope: Hosted frontier-model API for agents that need chat, responses, tool calling, embeddings, multimodal generation, realtime voice, files, evals, and project-level data controls.
entries.summary: OpenAI's hosted API platform for building agentic applications on GPT models, tools, embeddings, speech, images, and realtime interfaces.
entries.security_notes: Use project-scoped keys, org controls, ZDR where available, regional endpoints where required, spend limits, and strict tool/function boundaries.

data_residency.label: EU/UK/US+
data_residency.note: OpenAI documents API data residency per project across US, Europe, UK, and other regions; processing support varies by region, feature, and eligibility.

entries.name: Anthropic Claude API
entries.agent_native_scope: Hosted Claude API for agents that need long-context reasoning, tool use, files, code execution features, managed agents, batch work, and workspace-level policy controls.
entries.summary: Anthropic's hosted Claude API and cloud-platform routes for model calls, tool use, managed agents, and agentic application development.
entries.security_notes: Use workspaces, scoped API keys, ZDR where contracted, cloud-provider routes for specific compliance needs, and explicit tool-execution controls.

data_residency.label: US/global
data_residency.note: First-party Claude API workspace geo is currently US; supported newer models can route inference as US-only or global. Use Bedrock, Vertex, or Foundry when those provider regions are the control surface.

entries.name: Google Gemini API / Vertex AI
entries.agent_native_scope: Google Cloud model and agent platform for agents that need Gemini models, regional endpoints, tool use, multimodal generation, embeddings, RAG, evaluation, and enterprise cloud controls.
entries.summary: Google Cloud's Gemini and Vertex/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform surface for hosted models, agent building, regional endpoints, and enterprise AI controls.
entries.security_notes: Use project IAM, regional endpoints, VPC Service Controls, CMEK where supported, logging controls, and explicit checks for features excluded from residency commitments.

data_residency.label: Cloud region
data_residency.note: Google documents selected-location storage and regional or multi-regional ML processing for listed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform capabilities; unsupported endpoints do not guarantee in-region processing.

entries.name: Azure AI Foundry Models
entries.agent_native_scope: Microsoft Azure model platform for agents that need Azure OpenAI, Foundry Models, regional deployments, Agents, enterprise IAM, networking, and compliance controls.
entries.summary: Azure-hosted OpenAI and other Foundry Models for enterprise AI apps, with Azure deployment types, regional availability, and Microsoft data protection controls.
entries.security_notes: Choose deployment type deliberately: global, data-zone, and regional deployments have different processing boundaries. Use Azure IAM, private networking, content filters, and Azure policy controls.

data_residency.label: Azure geo
data_residency.note: Foundry deployment types distinguish global, data-zone, and regional processing; data at rest remains in the designated Azure geography for supported deployments.

entries.name: Amazon Bedrock
entries.agent_native_scope: AWS managed foundation-model and agents platform for model invocation, knowledge bases, guardrails, Bedrock Agents, tool use, evaluations, and enterprise cloud controls.
entries.summary: AWS's fully managed foundation-model platform for building and scaling generative AI and agentic applications across supported AWS Regions.
entries.security_notes: Use IAM least privilege, region controls, VPC/PrivateLink where appropriate, CloudTrail, guardrails, and geography-specific inference profiles for residency-sensitive workloads.

data_residency.label: AWS region
data_residency.note: Bedrock runs in AWS regions and supports geography-specific cross-region inference profiles such as US, EU, APAC, Japan, and Australia; model providers do not access Bedrock prompts or completions.

entries.name: Mistral AI La Plateforme

entries.security_notes: Choose EU default, US endpoint, partner-served, or self-hosted deployment deliberately. Review connector, code execution, document, and web-search tool data flows before use.

data_residency.label: EU default
data_residency.note: Mistral says data is hosted in the EU by default, with an explicit US API endpoint option and some feature-dependent transfers to listed subprocessors.

entries.name: Cohere Platform
entries.agent_native_scope: Enterprise model platform for agents that need Command, Embed, Rerank, Compass, tool-aware retrieval, private deployments, and secure model serving.
entries.summary: Cohere's enterprise AI platform and model APIs, with SaaS, isolated Model Vault, and customer-managed private deployment options.
entries.security_notes: Use private deployments or Model Vault for sensitive workloads, verify SaaS region/storage terms directly, and scope retrieval/reranking data carefully.

data_residency.label: Private deploy
data_residency.note: Cohere documents customer-managed private deployments where interactions remain in the customer's infrastructure; verify standard SaaS/API residency before sensitive use.

entries.name: GroqCloud
entries.agent_native_scope: Fast hosted inference platform for agents that need OpenAI-compatible chat, responses, audio, compound systems, built-in tools, and low-latency model calls.
entries.summary: Groq's hosted inference cloud for fast OpenAI-compatible model APIs, tool use, audio, and agentic compound systems.
entries.security_notes: Enable Zero Data Retention where appropriate, understand which features require application-state retention, and treat built-in web/code tools as privileged external actions.

data_residency.label: US storage
data_residency.note: Groq states customer data retained by GroqCloud is in GCP buckets located in the United States; ZDR can reduce retention for eligible features.

entries.name: Together AI
entries.agent_native_scope: AI-native cloud for agents that need serverless inference, dedicated inference, fine-tuning, GPU clusters, OpenAI-compatible APIs, speech, image, and multimodal model access.
entries.summary: Together AI's hosted platform for running, training, and serving open-source models through serverless, dedicated, and GPU-cluster options.
entries.security_notes: Use dedicated deployments for sensitive workloads, verify exact region/data residency terms with sales or docs, and avoid assuming serverless inference is region-pinned.

data_residency.label: Region options
data_residency.note: Together states global-region and dedicated data-residency options for enterprise deployments; exact countries/regions were not confirmed from a public technical residency page in this pass.

entries.name: Fireworks AI
entries.agent_native_scope: Hosted and dedicated inference platform for agents that need OpenAI-compatible APIs, low-latency model serving, on-demand deployments, fine-tuning, metrics, and regional placement.
entries.summary: Fireworks AI's inference and deployment platform for running open and custom models across global, US, Europe, and APAC region groupings.
entries.security_notes: Prefer explicit multi-region or single-region placement for residency needs, review serverless versus dedicated deployment behaviour, and monitor prompt/cache/metrics retention.

data_residency.label: Region choice
data_residency.note: Fireworks documents deployment multi-regions including GLOBAL, US, EUROPE, and APAC, with single-region availability by request or capacity.

entries.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
entries.agent_native_scope: Hosted model marketplace and API layer for agents that need access to many open and commercial inference providers through Hugging Face SDKs, Hub models, and endpoint routes.

entries.security_notes: Provider-specific data handling can differ. Verify the selected provider, endpoint region, storage region, logging, and model/license terms before sensitive use.

data_residency.label: EU/US choice
data_residency.note: Hugging Face documents EU storage regions for models, datasets, and inference endpoints; Inference Providers still require checking the chosen provider's handling.

entries.name: Replicate
entries.agent_native_scope: Hosted model API for agents that need quick access to image, video, audio, vision, document, and language models without managing inference infrastructure.
entries.summary: Replicate's cloud API for running community, official, and custom models, with predictable official models and API-based prediction workflows.
entries.security_notes: API prediction inputs and outputs are deleted after an hour by default, but web predictions persist. Treat third-party models, uploaded files, generated media, and webhook URLs as sensitive.

data_residency.label: US hosting
data_residency.note: Replicate's subprocessor list shows infrastructure and service subprocessors located in the United States; API prediction data is automatically removed after one hour by default.

entries.name: OpenRouter
entries.agent_native_scope: Model gateway for agents that need one API across many LLM providers, routing controls, privacy guardrails, ZDR enforcement, spend controls, and provider fallback.
entries.summary: OpenRouter is a hosted LLM routing gateway that gives agents a single API for many model providers with privacy, logging, routing, and enterprise controls.
entries.security_notes: Gateway routing means provider policies still matter. Use ZDR and provider logging settings, restrict allowed providers, and check which endpoints can satisfy residency or training restrictions.

data_residency.label: EU/ZDR route
data_residency.note: OpenRouter documents ZDR controls, provider logging controls, and sovereign/in-region routing, but each downstream provider's data policy still needs review.

entries.name: Fly.io GPUs and Machines
entries.agent_native_scope: Global app and GPU runtime for agents that need to host model-adjacent services, inference workers, tool servers, APIs, private networks, and regional microVMs close to users.
entries.summary: Fly.io runs apps, machines, volumes, and GPUs in selectable global regions, making it useful for agent services, inference-adjacent APIs, and low-latency hosted tools.
entries.security_notes: Pin machines and volumes to intended regions, avoid public exposure for internal agent tools, use secrets correctly, and remember that multi-region routing can move traffic if you configure it that way.

data_residency.label: Region choice
data_residency.note: Fly.io lists selectable regions including Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London, and several US regions; Fly Machines and Volumes are tied to the region where they are created.
